header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Accept wealth given to him

blocks.text: shivering from the cold. Hadhrat Antarah said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! You are shivering from cold when Allaah has allotted a share for you and your family from the wealth (of the state)?" Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "I swear by Allaah that I do not wish to take anything from the wealth of the people. I have even brought this shawl from my house in Madinah."[^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Accept wealth given to him
The Incident of Rasulullaah ﷺ With Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) and another Angel

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Allaah once sent to Rasulullaah ﷺ and angel with Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS). The angel said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "Allaah has given you a choice to either be a Nabi who is a slave (of Allaah) or a Nabi who is a king. Rasulullaah ﷺ turned to Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) to get his opinion. Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) indicated to Rasulullaah ﷺ that he should adopt humility. Rasulullaah ﷺ then replied, "I would rather be a Nabi who is a slave." After that day (like a true slave) Rasulullaah ﷺ never ate anything while reclining until the day he met Allaah.[^2]
Another Incident with Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) were once together on Mount Safa when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Jibra'eel! I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that the family of Muhammad have neither had a mouthful of flour nor a handful of porridge this evening." Rasulullaah ﷺ had barely completed his sentence when he was startled by a loud clamour from the sky. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Has Allaah given the command for Qiyaamah to take place?" "No," replied Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS), "Allaah has commanded Israafeel (AS) to come to you when he heard what you said." Hadhrat Israafeel (AS) then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "Allaah had heard what you said and has sent me with the keys to the treasures of the earth. Allaah has instructed me to make you the offer that if you wanted, I could transform the mountains of Tihaamah into emeralds, pearl, gold and silver and make them travel with you wherever you go. If you so wish, you could either be a Nabi who is a king or a Nabi who is a slave."
